interpretations.text: Sadness in a dream indicates joy and happiness in wakefulness. It is one of the opposites in interpretation. Whoever sees himself sad, God will relieve his worry.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Sadness indicates committing a sin that causes worry. Whoever sees himself sad will soon be happy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Sadness is interpreted as joy. Whoever sees himself consoling a sad person will receive a great reward.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Jealousy in a dream indicates keenness on religion and worldly life. A man's jealousy over his wife indicates his love and protection for her. A woman's jealousy indicates corruption in her religion.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Jealousy indicates love. It may also indicate falling into strife because of women. The jealousy of a ruler indicates his justice and protection of his subjects.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Jealousy is interpreted as keenness on what one possesses. Praiseworthy jealousy is righteousness in religion, and blameworthy jealousy is corruption and obsessive suspicion.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Regret in a dream indicates repentance and returning to God. Whoever sees himself regretting a sin, God will forgive him. Regretting a good deed indicates loss.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Regret indicates salvation from perils. Whoever sees himself regretful will fall into a matter he regrets in wakefulness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Regret is interpreted as repentance. Whoever sees himself regretting selling something is attached to the world and abandoning the Hereafter.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The city in a dream indicates a scholar or a ruler. A prosperous city indicates a scholar who acts upon his knowledge. A ruined city indicates a scholar who does not act upon his knowledge or an unjust ruler.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The city indicates the world. Entering an unknown city indicates the approach of death for the sick. Building a city indicates the gathering of scholars and righteous people.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The city is interpreted as the king and the scholar. A fortified city indicates security and invincibility. Whoever sees himself moving from one city to another, his situation will change.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The village in a dream indicates its people. Its prosperity is the prosperity of its people, and its ruin indicates strife, death, or injustice that befalls them.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An unknown village indicates worry and grief. Entering an unjust village indicates falling into hardship. Exiting it is salvation.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The village is interpreted as injustice and strife. Whoever sees himself in a village will fall into worry proportional to its ruin or prosperity.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The market in a dream indicates the mosque or the battlefield. Profit in the market is jihad (struggle), and loss is the opposite. An unknown market indicates being lost and confused.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The market indicates the world, heedlessness, and strife. Buying and selling in it indicates eagerness for the world. Each market has an interpretation according to what is sold in it.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The market is interpreted as seeking livelihood. A bustling market indicates sustenance and benefit, and stagnation indicates unemployment and poverty.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The mosque in a dream is a knowledgeable man or a just ruler. Entering the mosque indicates security, knowledge, and guidance. Building a mosque indicates enjoining good and forbidding evil.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The mosque indicates justice, judgment, and the market. Whoever sees his house turn into a mosque will gain honor and high status. Whoever sees a mosque demolished, a scholar or ruler has died in that place.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The mosque is interpreted as the king, the scholar, or the righteous wife. Praying in it is the fulfillment of a need. Sleeping in it indicates trust in God.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The church in a dream indicates a house of knowledge for scholars, or a house of worry and grief for the ignorant. It may also indicate a grave, a prison, or a house of heresy.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The church indicates a lying woman or a heretical man. Entering it indicates marriage for the unmarried, a child for the pregnant, or falling into worry.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The church is interpreted as the king's house or a man of position. Whoever sees himself praying in it is drawing close to the ruler.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The shirt in a dream is a man's religion, his world, or his work. A new, wide shirt indicates righteousness in religion and abundance in the world. A torn shirt indicates separation or divorce. A wet shirt is a difficult journey. Joseph's (Yusuf's) shirt is good news of relief, salvation, and healing for the eyes.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The shirt indicates a man's condition. Whoever sees himself wear a new shirt will get married if unmarried or be blessed with a son. Whoever sees his shirt without a sleeve is a poor man who owns nothing.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The shirt is interpreted as the man, and whatever good or bad is seen in it reflects on him. A white shirt is religion and piety, green is martyrdom, and black is worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Trousers in a dream indicate a foreign woman or a maidservant. Whoever buys new trousers will marry a virgin. If the trousers are of silk, he is a man who wears the unlawful and commits debauchery.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Trousers indicate chastity and salvation from an ugly matter. Wearing them indicates a man's modesty. Whoever sees himself urinating in his trousers, his wife will become pregnant.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Trousers are interpreted as a woman. Whatever good or bad is seen in them reflects on her. Clean trousers indicate the wife's righteousness, and dirty ones her corruption.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The hat (Qalansuwa) in a dream indicates a man's superior, his authority, or his wife. Its newness and beauty indicate the high status of the superior or the beauty of the wife. Its falling indicates separation from the superior or wife.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The hat indicates travel, marriage, or authority. Whoever wears it will get what he seeks. If it is dirty, it is worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The hat is interpreted as prestige and position. A white one is religion and righteousness, green is martyrdom, and black is leadership and wealth.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The minaret in a dream is a righteous man who calls people to goodness and guidance. Climbing it indicates gaining authority and high status. Its fall indicates the death of a scholar or the scattering of a group.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The minaret indicates the messenger, the Imam, or the Muezzin. Whoever sees himself calling the Adhan from a minaret, his status will rise and his reputation will spread.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The minaret is interpreted as the king or a great man. Building it indicates a righteous work that unites people. Its demolition indicates the death of the king.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The pulpit in a dream indicates a ruler, a scholar, or an orator. Ascending it indicates gaining authority and high status if he is worthy. Otherwise, it indicates a scandal or crucifixion.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The pulpit indicates a high position. Delivering a sermon from it indicates enjoining good and forbidding evil. Descending from it indicates dismissal.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The pulpit is interpreted as the king or the vizier. A pulpit of wood indicates authority from a hypocritical man. Whoever sees himself fall from the pulpit will be dismissed from his position.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The mihrab in a dream indicates the Imam of the Muslims or their leader. It is a place of obedience and worship. Praying in it indicates good religion and the glad tidings of a righteous son.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The mihrab indicates a righteous wife or authority. Whoever sees himself praying in a mihrab will be blessed with a blessed baby boy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The mihrab is interpreted as a righteous man. Entering it indicates security and guidance. Whoever sees himself building a mihrab is establishing a righteous work.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The hermitage in a dream indicates Islam or the king. Whoever sees himself in a hermitage will gain security and high status.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The hermitage indicates a righteous man who isolates himself from people. Its demolition indicates the death of an ascetic scholar.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The hermitage is interpreted as a righteous woman. Whoever sees himself building a hermitage will marry a righteous woman or be blessed with a righteous son.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The fortress in a dream is religion and knowledge that fortifies its owner. Entering it indicates adherence to religion and salvation from strife.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The fortress indicates an invincible man or a ruler. It is security from fear. Whoever sees himself building a fortress is fortifying his religion or his world.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The fortress is interpreted as the king or the scholar. Entering it indicates marriage to a fortified virgin woman.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The wall in a dream is a ruler or an invincible man who protects people. The wall surrounding the city indicates its ruler. Its demolition indicates the ruler's death.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The wall indicates a partner or a neighbor. Walking on it indicates adherence to religion. Falling from it indicates falling into sin.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The wall is interpreted as the king or ruler. Its strength is the king's strength, and its weakness is the king's weakness.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The trench in a dream indicates a man who protects his family and wealth. It may also indicate travel. Falling into it indicates falling into cunning or hardship.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The trench indicates a difficult matter that cannot be overcome except with hardship. Crossing it indicates salvation from hardship.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The trench is interpreted as worry and grief. Getting out of it is relief and salvation.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The room in a dream indicates the wife. Its beauty and spaciousness indicate the wife's beauty and good character. It may also indicate security from fear.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The room indicates the world. Whoever sees himself in a decorated room will gain a spacious world. An unknown room indicates the grave.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The room is interpreted as a woman. A high room is high status and honor. Whoever sees himself building a room will marry a woman and collect wealth.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The ceiling in a dream is a man of high status. If it is of wood, he is an arrogant man. Its collapse indicates a calamity from a great man or the death of the house's owner.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The ceiling indicates the father, the husband, or the master. Whatever bad happens to it reflects on them. Whoever sees water dripping from the ceiling, it is crying and worry.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The ceiling is interpreted as the man. A high ceiling indicates high status, and a low one indicates lowliness. Whoever sees a snake descending from the ceiling, it is an enemy from the ruler.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The pillar in a dream is religion or the man who is relied upon. A pillar of iron indicates a strong ruler. Its fall indicates the death of whomever it represents.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The pillar indicates the governor, the father, or the husband. Whoever sees himself carrying a pillar is bearing a great responsibility.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The pillar is interpreted as the king or a noble man. A short pillar indicates a short life. A pillar of light indicates a righteous scholar.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The stairs (ladder) in a dream indicate the means of elevation in religion and worldly life. Ascending them indicates gaining high status, and descending them indicates a decline.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Stairs indicate travel or a servant. Stairs of clay indicate authority with righteousness in religion, and of wood indicate authority with hypocrisy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Stairs are interpreted as safety and victory. Ascending them is elevation, and descending them is a decline. Falling from them indicates failure and loss.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The window in a dream is honor and high status for whoever looks from it. It indicates learning of secrets and the arrival of news. A new window is marriage for the unmarried.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The window indicates a woman who looks at people or a man who spies on his neighbors. Exiting through it indicates falling into heresy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The window is interpreted as news coming from the direction one is looking. An open window is relief, and a closed one is worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The door in a dream is the caretaker of the house and the manager of its affairs. The door of the house indicates the man's wife. An open door means the doors of sustenance and relief, and a closed one is the opposite. Removing the door indicates divorcing the wife.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The door indicates knowledge, sustenance, and relief. Exiting from a narrow door to a wide one is relief from worry and grief. A new door is a new wife or a new partner.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The door is interpreted as the head of the household. Changing the door indicates a change in the state of the house's owner. A burnt door indicates a calamity for the wife.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The chair in a dream is authority, high status, and power. Sitting on a chair indicates marriage for the unmarried, or travel, or gaining authority. Falling from it indicates dismissal from a position.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The chair indicates a noble woman or a maidservant. For a pregnant woman, it is a baby boy. A chair of iron indicates a strong, powerful man.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The chair is interpreted as high status and a high position. Whoever sees himself sitting on a chair will gain a proxy or guardianship.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The bed in a dream indicates the wife, comfort, and authority. Sitting on an unknown bed indicates gaining kingship or death for the sick. A broken bed indicates the death of the wife or the loss of authority.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The bed indicates everything a person finds comfort in, such as a wife, a house, or authority. A wide bed indicates abundant sustenance and the good state of the wife.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The bed is interpreted as a woman, high status, and joy. Whoever sees himself carrying his bed will travel and gain high status on his journey.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The earth in a dream indicates the wife or the world. Its vastness is the vastness of the dreamer's world. The earth swallowing the dreamer indicates his travel or his death. Plowing the earth indicates marriage.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The earth indicates a woman or a partner. Whoever sees himself owning vast land, his world will expand. Whoever sees the earth speaking, a great strife will occur.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The earth is interpreted as a woman. Plants growing from it indicate her pregnancy. Its dryness indicates her infertility. Whoever sees himself eating from the earth will gain wealth proportional to what he ate.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Soil (dust) in a dream indicates people. Collecting soil indicates collecting money. Walking on soil is striving to seek sustenance. Soil on the head indicates a calamity and worry.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Soil indicates the world and its people. Eating soil is poverty and need. Whoever shakes the soil off his hands will become poor.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Soil is interpreted as wealth and benefit. Whoever sees himself digging the earth and taking out its soil will gain wealth through cunning.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Stones in a dream indicate hard hearts and ignorant men. Carrying a stone indicates bearing harm from an ignorant man. Throwing stones indicates slander and gossip.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A stone indicates a patient man. Precious stones indicate scholars and righteous people. Striking a stone with a stone indicates a dispute with a hard-hearted man.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: A stone is interpreted as a man who is solid in his religion or his world. Whoever sees himself collecting stones is collecting money with fatigue.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Glass in a dream indicates women. It is worry and grief because it cannot withstand heat or cold. Breaking it indicates a scandal or the revealing of a secret.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Glass indicates matters that do not last. It may also indicate hypocrisy and pretense. Colored glass indicates adorned women.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Glass is interpreted as worry. Whoever sees himself being wounded by glass will be afflicted with worry from a woman.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Paper (for writing) in a dream indicates the fulfillment of needs and achieving goals. White paper indicates purity of state. Writing on it indicates cunning and deceit.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Paper indicates knowledge and understanding. Eating written paper indicates memorizing knowledge. Whoever sees himself writing on paper is giving testimony.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Paper is interpreted as wealth and sustenance. Whoever sees a paper in his hand will gain wealth or knowledge.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The pen in a dream is authority, knowledge, and command. Whoever sees a pen in his hand will be blessed with a knowledgeable son or gain authority. Writing with a pen indicates the fulfillment of needs.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The pen indicates what a person is known for, such as knowledge or a craft. Whoever sees himself sharpening a pen is planning a great matter.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The pen is interpreted as knowledge, wisdom, and a male child. Whoever sees his pen break, his son will die or his knowledge will vanish.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The inkwell in a dream is the manager of the scholar's or ruler's affairs. For a woman, it is a husband. Whoever sees himself writing from an inkwell will gain knowledge and sustenance.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The inkwell indicates a woman or a servant. The ink in it indicates a child or wealth. Its dryness indicates poverty or infertility.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The inkwell is interpreted as a noble man who strives for good. Whoever sees an inkwell and a pen in his hand will gain authority and a high position.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The wind in a dream is torment, authority, or illness. A good, gentle wind is glad tidings, goodness, and healing. A strong, stormy wind indicates strife, an epidemic, or injustice from the ruler. Whoever sees the wind carry him will gain authority and high status if he is worthy; otherwise, it indicates a severe illness.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The wind indicates the ruler's soldiers or his commands. Wind that carries soil or dust indicates war and strife. Wind that pollinates trees indicates fertility and prosperity.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The wind is interpreted as glad tidings or torment. Gentle winds are sustenance, relief, and healing. Strong winds are worry, grief, and illness. Whoever sees the wind enter his house will gain authority.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Trees in a dream indicate men and women of different types and natures. A good, fruit-bearing tree indicates a faithful, generous, and beneficial man. A bad tree indicates a disbelieving, harmful man. Cutting a tree indicates the death of a sick person or the severing of family ties.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A tree indicates one's work and lifespan. Planting a tree indicates marrying into a noble family and gaining honor. An unknown tree indicates worry and grief. Sitting under a tree indicates relying on a generous man.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The tree is interpreted as a man. Whatever good or bad is seen in it reflects on him. A dry tree is a poor or hypocritical man. Whoever sees that he owns many trees will gain authority over men.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Oil in a dream is lawful money, blessed sustenance, light, and guidance. Olive oil is knowledge, blessing, and healing. Drinking oil indicates magic or illness. Anointing the body with oil indicates the removal of worry and healing.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Oil indicates the light of insight and lawful sustenance. Whoever sees himself eating bread with oil will live a pleasant, blessed life. Murky oil is worry and illness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Oil is interpreted as lawful money and blessing. Whoever sees himself pressing olives will receive abundant goodness after fatigue.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Butter in a dream is spoils, fertility, and lawful sustenance. Eating it indicates healing for the sick and blessing in sustenance.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Butter indicates useful knowledge and abundant sustenance. For a student, it is success, and for a merchant, profit.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Butter is interpreted as wealth collected from a lawful source. Whoever sees himself gathering butter is collecting money for his family.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Fat in a dream indicates wealth, fertility, and goodness. Eating it indicates eating from a noble man's wealth. Fat from a dead animal is unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Fat indicates knowledge for scholars and marriage for the unmarried. It may also indicate an adulterous woman.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Fat is interpreted as wealth and benefit. Whoever sees himself melting fat is spending money on a good cause.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Bones in a dream are a man's foundation in his wealth and religion. Breaking a bone indicates illness or calamity. Collecting bones indicates collecting money or striving to build.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Bones indicate family and clan. Their strength is the family's strength, and their weakness is their weakness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Bones are interpreted as stored wealth. Whoever sees himself eating a bone will gain wealth from a stingy man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Brain (or marrow) in a dream is buried wealth and hidden knowledge. Eating it indicates gaining stored wealth or hidden knowledge.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The brain indicates the mind and prudence. Whoever sees that he has no brain is an ignorant, foolish man.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The brain is interpreted as wealth. Whoever sees himself taking out a person's brain is seizing his wealth.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The horn in a dream is a man's strength, his defense, and his weapon. The strength of the horns indicates the strength of the ruler. A broken horn indicates the loss of position or humiliation.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The horn indicates a year, a son, or wealth. Whoever sees that he has horns like a bull's horns will gain authority and prestige.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The horn is interpreted as strength and defense. Whoever sees an animal strike him with its horn will be harmed by a strong man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Feathers in a dream are wealth, leadership, and adornment. Whoever sees feathers on himself will gain wealth and prestige. Plucking feathers indicates the loss of wealth and prestige.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Feathers indicate goodness and benefit. White feathers indicate righteousness in religion, and black ones indicate leadership and wealth.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Feathers are interpreted as wealth. Whoever sees himself collecting feathers is collecting money from various sources.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A bird's beak in a dream indicates its tongue and its speech. Its strength indicates the man's eloquence. Its breaking indicates his inability to speak.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The beak indicates knowledge and argument. Whoever sees a bird pecking him will hear words that harm him.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The beak is interpreted as a man who argues and disputes a lot. Whoever sees that his beak is long, his tongue is long with evil.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The claw in a dream is a man's weapon and his strength. The strength of the claw indicates the man's strength in facing his enemies.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The claw indicates adherence to religion or a position. Whoever sees that he has claws, his authority will strengthen and he will overcome his enemies.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The claw is interpreted as strength and victory. Whoever sees an animal scratch him with its claw will be harmed by an enemy.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A bird's nest in a dream is a man's house and his wife. Whoever sees a nest with eggs or chicks will be blessed with children or wealth.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The nest indicates a person's shelter and dwelling. An empty nest indicates an abandoned house or worry and sadness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The nest is interpreted as the wife. Whoever sees himself building a nest will marry a woman and unite his family.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The branch in a dream indicates children, brothers, and relatives. A green branch indicates a righteous son. A dry one indicates the death of a relative.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The branch indicates a partner or a friend. Cutting it indicates separating from a partner or severing family ties.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The branch is interpreted as a son. Whoever sees himself breaking a branch is being undutiful to or harming his son.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Tree leaves in a dream indicate covering (concealment) and wealth. Green leaves indicate righteousness in religion and lawful sustenance. Yellow leaves indicate illness and worry.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Tree leaves indicate clothes. Their falling indicates the loss of wealth or the approach of death.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Leaves are interpreted as wealth. Whoever sees himself collecting tree leaves is collecting money.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The root of a tree in a dream indicates a man's origin and his religion. Its strength indicates the strength of his religion. Uprooting it indicates abandoning religion or moving from a country.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The root indicates secrets and hidden matters. Whoever sees tree roots exposed, secrets will be revealed to him.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The root is interpreted as a person's origin and lineage. Whoever sees himself uprooting a tree root is severing his family ties.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Planting in a dream indicates work and striving. Whoever plants and harvests will reap the fruit of his labor. Whoever plants in land that is not his is committing adultery.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Planting indicates marriage and pregnancy. Green crops indicate a long life and righteous work. Dry crops indicate the approach of death.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Planting is interpreted as wealth and sustenance. Whoever sees himself planting crops will gain honor and a son.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Harvesting crops in their season indicates goodness, sustenance, and justice. Out of season, it indicates war, death, or strife.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The harvest indicates the end of one matter and the beginning of another. For a merchant, it is profit, and for the sick, death.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The harvest is interpreted as spoils and wealth. Whoever sees himself harvesting another's crops will be afflicted with harm.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The garden (Bustan) in a dream is the wife. Whatever good or bad happens in the garden reflects on her. Watering the garden indicates intimacy with the wife. An unknown garden is Paradise.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The garden indicates seeking forgiveness and repentance. Entering it for the unmarried is marriage, and for the sick, healing. A dry garden indicates a barren woman.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The garden is interpreted as a wife, wealth, a child, and a good life. Whoever sees himself strolling in a garden, his worry and grief will disappear.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The desert (wasteland) in a dream indicates dangerous matters or a journey with fatigue. Getting lost in it is confusion in religion or worldly life. Whoever sees himself alone in it will travel alone.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The desert indicates poverty and unemployment or an unjust ruler. Exiting it is salvation from worry and hardship.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The desert is interpreted as travel or a woman of ill repute. Whoever sees crops or water in it will receive good from an unexpected source.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The valley in a dream indicates travel, a righteous deed, or hardship. Crossing it indicates salvation from worry. Running in it indicates wading into strife.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The valley indicates a generous or a stingy man, depending on its state. A green valley indicates a righteous deed, and a dry one indicates a false deed.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The valley is interpreted as the king or a great man. Descending into it indicates drawing close to the ruler.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The hill in a dream is a man of high status or a scholar. Ascending it indicates gaining high status and position. Descending from it indicates a decline.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The hill indicates a noble woman. Sitting on it indicates empowerment and victory. A green hill indicates a righteous man.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The hill is interpreted as collected wealth. Whoever sees that he owns a hill owns abundant wealth.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The cave in a dream is a shelter, a refuge, and security from fear. Entering it indicates salvation from enemies. For the prisoner, it is relief, and for the sick, healing.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The cave indicates a long life. It may also indicate hiding secrets. Whoever sees himself in a cave is seeking refuge with a great man.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The cave is interpreted as a servant, a father, or a wife. A dark cave indicates worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Clouds in a dream indicate Islam, knowledge, and wisdom. Clouds with no rain indicate a ruler who does not benefit. Black clouds indicate worry and hardship.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Clouds indicate soldiers or travel. Whoever sees a cloud covering the sun, the ruler will fall ill or his situation will change.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Clouds are interpreted as the king or the scholar. White clouds indicate righteousness in work, and black ones indicate its corruption.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Fog in a dream indicates strife, confusion, and doubt in religion. Walking in it indicates delving into a matter whose outcome is unclear.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Fog indicates deceit and cunning. Whoever sees the fog clear will have a hidden matter revealed to him.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Fog is interpreted as worry and grief. Exiting from it is relief and salvation.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Dew in a dream indicates sustenance, blessing, and good speech. For the sick, it is healing, and for the worried, relief.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Dew indicates familiarity and love. Whoever sees dew on crops, it indicates fertility and prosperity.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Dew is interpreted as goodness and benefit. Walking on it indicates striving for a blessed matter.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Musk in a dream indicates joy, wealth, and prestige. For a pregnant woman, it is a baby boy. Whoever perfumes himself with musk, his reputation for good will spread.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Musk indicates a beautiful maidservant or useful knowledge. Whoever sees musk in his hand will gain spoils and lawful wealth.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Musk is interpreted as good praise and wealth. Whoever smells the scent of musk will hear good news.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Ambergris in a dream is noble wealth from a noble man. Whoever perfumes himself with it will gain good praise from people.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Ambergris indicates a generous man or useful knowledge. For a merchant, it is profit, and for a scholar, fame.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Ambergris is interpreted as wealth and benefit. Whoever finds ambergris has found a treasure or received an inheritance.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Incense in a dream is good praise and a beautiful memory. Whoever sees himself perfuming with incense, his reputation for good will spread. For the sick, incense is healing.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Incense indicates the fulfillment of needs and the removal of worry. Its good scent indicates hearing good news.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Incense is interpreted as reconciliation between disputants. Whoever sees himself buying incense is striving for reconciliation.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Saffron in a dream is good praise. It may also indicate illness because it is yellow. Whoever drinks it will fall ill. Whoever sees himself dye his garment with saffron will fall seriously ill.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Saffron indicates joy and happiness if it does not touch the body. If it does, it is illness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Saffron is interpreted as good praise. Eating it indicates gaining wealth after fatigue and illness.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The rose in a dream indicates a child, noble wealth, or a trade that does not last. Picking it indicates joy and happiness. A white rose indicates a chaste woman.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The rose indicates a noble man or a beautiful woman. Smelling it indicates kissing a woman or a child. A withered rose indicates illness or separation.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The rose is interpreted as joy and delight. Whoever sees a crown of roses on his head will marry a beautiful woman, then separate from her quickly.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Jasmine in a dream is joy, happiness, and good praise. It indicates a beautiful, chaste woman.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Jasmine indicates a scholar or a righteous man. Picking it indicates gaining knowledge from a scholar.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Jasmine is interpreted as marriage to a beautiful woman. Smelling it indicates hearing good news.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Basil (Rayhan) in a dream indicates a child, knowledge, or a wife. For the sick, it is healing, and for the worried, relief.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Basil indicates good speech and good praise. Smelling it indicates comfort and joy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Basil is interpreted as a righteous son. Picking it indicates a small worry followed by joy.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The narcissus in a dream indicates a beautiful woman. It is joy and happiness that do not last.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The narcissus indicates wealth, gold, and silver. Picking it indicates kissing a beautiful maidservant.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The narcissus is interpreted as a beautiful woman. Whoever sees a crown of it on his head will marry a beautiful woman.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The violet in a dream indicates a beautiful, pious maidservant. Picking it indicates kissing her.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The violet indicates a humble scholar or a righteous woman. It is joy and happiness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The violet is interpreted as a righteous woman. Smelling it indicates hearing good words.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Myrtle in a dream is a man who is faithful to his covenant. It indicates the stability and permanence of matters.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Myrtle indicates a permanent wife or a surviving child. For the sick, it is healing.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Myrtle is interpreted as a righteous man. Whoever sees a crown of it on his head will gain lasting authority.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Henna in a dream indicates adornment in wealth and children. For men, it indicates concealment in matters. Dyeing the beard indicates following the Sunnah.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Henna indicates joy and happiness. Dyeing the hands and feet for a woman indicates her husband's good treatment of her.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Henna is interpreted as wealth and prestige. Whoever sees himself dyeing his hand will triumph over his enemy.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Kohl in a dream is wealth, an increase in insight, and righteousness in religion. For the unmarried, it is marriage. For the poor, it is wealth.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Kohl indicates knowledge and light. Whoever sees himself applying kohl is seeking righteousness in his religion. For a woman, kohl is a righteous husband.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Kohl is interpreted as wealth. Whoever sees himself applying kohl (ithmid) will marry two women.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Ointment (or oil/fat) in a dream is wealth and adornment. A good-smelling ointment indicates good praise. A bad-smelling ointment indicates ugly praise.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Ointment indicates healing from illnesses. Anointing the head indicates the removal of worry. Anointing the body indicates adornment.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Ointment is interpreted as lawful money. Whoever sees himself anointing his head is reforming the affairs of his superior.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Soap in a dream is wealth that removes worry. Washing clothes with soap indicates repentance, payment of debt, and healing from illnesses.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Soap indicates the removal of worries and troubles. Eating it indicates consuming unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Soap is interpreted as a man who removes people's worries. Whoever sees himself washing with soap is purifying himself from his sins.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The comb in a dream is a beneficial, just man or a scholar. Combing hair with it indicates the removal of worry and healing from illness. Combing the beard indicates following the Sunnah.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The comb indicates joy and happiness. For a merchant, it is profit, and for a farmer, fertility.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The comb is interpreted as a knowledgeable man. Whoever sees himself combing his hair is getting rid of debts and worries.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The tent in a dream is authority, a high position, or a wife. Whoever sees himself in a tent will gain authority and high status. A white tent indicates a righteous man, and a green one indicates a fertile year.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The tent indicates travel or the grave. Entering it for the unmarried is marriage. Whoever sees himself exiting his tent will lose his authority.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The tent is interpreted as the king or a great man. Whoever sees that he owns many tents will gain a great kingdom.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The large tent (Fustat) in a dream is kingship and authority. Whoever sees a pavilion set up for him will gain kingship and prestige. Its collapse indicates the loss of kingship.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The pavilion indicates a righteous man. Entering it indicates security and salvation.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The pavilion is interpreted as the king. Whoever sees that he has a pavilion will gain great authority.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A weapon in a dream is victory over enemies and healing from illnesses. Whoever sees himself armed will gain a position and high status. For a sick person, a weapon indicates his death.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A weapon indicates the wife with whom a man fortifies himself. Whoever sees himself selling his weapon is losing his religion and his world.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: A weapon is interpreted as strength and defense. Whoever sees himself carrying a weapon among unarmed people will become their leader.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Armor in a dream is a fortress against enemies and protection from affliction. Wearing it indicates gaining authority or a righteous brother to rely on.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Armor indicates an invincible man who protects his family. For a woman, it is a husband who protects her.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Armor is interpreted as security and salvation. Whoever sees himself wearing armor is safe from his fear.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The spear in a dream is a male child, a brother, or travel. Stabbing with it indicates slandering people. Its breaking indicates the death of the son or brother.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The spear indicates a brave man. Whoever sees a spear in his hand will gain authority or be blessed with a son.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The spear is interpreted as a son. Whoever sees his spear grow long, his son's life will be long.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The bow in a dream is travel, a son, a wife, or strength. Shooting the bow indicates sending a messenger or impactful speech. Its breaking indicates a difficult journey or the death of whomever it represents.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The bow indicates a man who settles matters between people. For a woman, it is a husband. Whoever sees himself drawing a bow will be blessed with a baby boy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The bow is interpreted as travel. A bent bow indicates the gathering of brothers.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The shield (Turs/Darqa) in a dream is a man who protects his friend from enemies, like a brother or a friend. It is protection from affliction.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The shield indicates a righteous man who prevents evil. Whoever sees a shield in his hand will be saved from his enemy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The shield is interpreted as a brother or a friend. Whoever sees his shield break, his brother or friend will die.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The helmet (literally 'egg') in a dream is security from fear, authority, and prestige. Wearing it indicates gaining authority or marrying a noble woman.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The helmet indicates a strong man who protects his family. For a woman, it is a husband.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The helmet is interpreted as the king or a noble man. Whoever sees himself wearing it will gain security and high status.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The banner in a dream is a scholar, an Imam, or a brave man who is followed. Whoever sees a banner in his hand will gain honor and authority. A black banner indicates a jurist scholar, and a red one indicates a man of war.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The banner indicates marriage for the unmarried. For a woman, it is a husband. Its fall indicates the death of whomever it represents.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The banner is interpreted as the king or a great man. Whoever sees himself following a banner is following an Imam.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Pearls in a dream indicate the Quran and knowledge. Whoever sees himself drilling a pearl is interpreting the Quran correctly. Scattered pearls indicate children or servants. Swallowing pearls indicates concealing knowledge and wisdom.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Pearls indicate an inheritance or lawful money. Whoever sees himself buying pearls has bought a beautiful maidservant or learned useful knowledge. A single pearl indicates a baby boy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Pearls are interpreted as a beautiful woman or a righteous son. Whoever sees himself emitting pearls from his mouth is speaking good words and wisdom.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Coral in a dream indicates abundant wealth and a noble man. Whoever sees himself wearing something made of coral will gain wealth from a beautiful woman.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Coral indicates a beautiful wife or a maidservant. A necklace of it indicates authority and wealth.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Coral is interpreted as lawful money. Whoever sees himself collecting it is collecting money from multiple sources.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Ruby in a dream is joy, happiness, and knowledge. For a woman, it is a son. Whoever sees that he owns a ruby will gain knowledge and high status. A single ruby indicates a beautiful woman.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Ruby indicates wisdom and knowledge. Wearing it indicates prestige and dignity. Whoever finds a ruby will marry a righteous woman.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Ruby is interpreted as a beautiful woman or a righteous son. A red ruby indicates an adorned woman, and a yellow one indicates a sick woman.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Emerald in a dream indicates lawful money and a righteous son. Whoever wears it as a ring will attain martyrdom or authority.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Emerald indicates a brave man or a loyal friend. It indicates useful knowledge.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Emerald is interpreted as a righteous woman. Whoever sees that he owns one has befriended a noble man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Copper in a dream is wealth from non-Arabs. Utensils made of it indicate a loyal servant. Whoever sees himself melting copper is disputing over a false matter.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Copper indicates bad speech and gossip. Working with it indicates falling into a disliked matter.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Copper is interpreted as unlawful money. Whoever sees himself selling it is getting rid of a worry.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Lead in a dream is lowly money and a treacherous servant. Whoever sees himself melting it will fall victim to people's tongues and dispute over a matter with no good in it.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Lead indicates weak people with no strength. It may also indicate the stability of matters.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Lead is interpreted as unlawful money. Whoever sees himself working with it is striving for a false matter.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The scales in a dream indicate the judge, the scholar, or religion and justice. Its balance indicates the straightness of religion and justice. Its tilting indicates injustice and misguidance.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The scales indicate guidance. Whoever sees scales in his hand is on the path of truth. The beam of the scales is the tongue of truth.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The scales are interpreted as the king or ruler. What is weighed with it indicates judgments. Whoever sees his scale tip in his favor, his argument is stronger.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The lock in a dream is a trustworthy man, religion, or an argument. Opening it indicates the facilitation of matters and the removal of worry. An iron lock is a knowledgeable man, and a wooden one is a hypocritical man.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The lock indicates a virgin woman for the unmarried. It may also indicate heedlessness and misguidance. Opening a lock is relief from worry and payment of debt.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The lock is interpreted as a guardian. Whoever sees himself opening a lock will get married or his worry will be relieved.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The chain in a dream indicates religion, a righteous wife, or a child. Whoever sees himself bound by a chain is steadfast in his religion. It may also indicate worry and sin.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The chain indicates torment and worry. Whoever sees himself in a chain will fall into hardship. A chain on the neck is a debt or a trust.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The chain is interpreted as sin. Whoever sees himself breaking a chain is repenting from a sin.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The oven in a dream is the ruler's house or a place for fulfilling needs. A hot oven indicates a house full of goodness. A cold one indicates unemployment and poverty.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The oven indicates the owner of the house and the manager of its affairs. It is a place of sustenance and benefit. Whoever sees himself building an oven will get married or gain authority.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The oven is interpreted as a rich, generous man. Whoever sees himself baking in it will receive blessed sustenance.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Ash in a dream is unlawful money or false, useless speech. Collecting it indicates striving for a false matter. Falling into it indicates worry from a ruler.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Ash indicates knowledge that is not acted upon. It may also indicate dispute and evil.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Ash is interpreted as worry and grief. Whoever sees himself cleaning up ash is getting rid of a worry.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Coal in a dream is unlawful money from a ruler or a dangerous man. If it is not glowing (embers), it is an ominous man.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Coal indicates sustenance in which there is doubt. Whoever sees himself carrying coal is bearing a sin.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Coal is interpreted as a man of bad character. Burning coal indicates strife and war.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A flame in a dream indicates hardship and strife. A flame with no smoke indicates closeness to the ruler. A flame with a sound indicates war and dispute.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A flame indicates high prices and an epidemic. Whoever sees a flame coming out of his house, strife has occurred in it.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: A flame is interpreted as torment and worry. Whoever sees himself eating a flame is consuming unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Rust in a dream is corruption in religion and committing sins. Rust on a sword indicates an unrighteous son. Rust on a mirror indicates the bad state of the wife.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Rust indicates people of heresy and misguidance. Whoever sees himself removing rust is repenting from a sin.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Rust is interpreted as a hypocritical man. Whoever sees that one of his belongings is rusty is befriending a bad man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The mill in a dream indicates war, dispute, or travel. Its turning indicates the continuation of the matter. Its stopping indicates the stopping of one's situation.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The mill indicates a man who unites people. It may also indicate a wife or a servant.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The mill is interpreted as sustenance and livelihood. Whoever sees himself grinding with it will gain sustenance with fatigue.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The millstone in a dream indicates a scholar or a ruler. It may also indicate a husband and wife. Its turning indicates travel and sustenance.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The millstone indicates death, war, or hardship. Whoever sees himself grinding with it will fall into hardship.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The millstone is interpreted as sustenance. The flour from it is lawful money.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Flour in a dream is collected lawful money and immediate sustenance. Wheat flour indicates justice and fertility, and barley flour indicates religion and piety.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Flour indicates useful knowledge. Kneading it indicates an impending journey.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Flour is interpreted as lawful money. Whoever sees himself selling it is selling his religion for his world.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Dough in a dream is honorable wealth and lawful sustenance from trade. Leavened dough indicates the approach of relief and profit. Unleavened dough indicates haste and worry.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Dough indicates imminent relief. Kneading flour indicates travel. Dough in the house indicates collected wealth.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Dough is interpreted as goodness and blessing. Whoever sees himself kneading is striving for a matter from which he will earn.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Yeast in a dream is money that grows and increases. Whoever sees himself putting it in dough will gain a profit in his trade.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Yeast indicates blessing in wealth and children. Dough without yeast is money that does not grow.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: Yeast is interpreted as lawful money. Whoever sees himself eating it will fall ill.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The mare in a dream is a free, noble woman. Whoever rides her will marry a righteous woman. Whoever dismounts from her will separate from her. Her death indicates the wife's death.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The mare indicates a wife, a house, or a partner. A beautiful mare indicates a world approaching with goodness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The mare is interpreted as a woman. Whoever sees that he owns a mare will receive good from a woman.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The mule in a dream is a sterile man or a long journey. Riding it indicates a long life. A white mule indicates a religious man, and a black one indicates a rich man.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The mule indicates a child of adultery (from zina). It may also indicate a man of no origin.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The mule is interpreted as travel. Whoever sees himself riding it will travel far.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The ox in a dream is a brave, strong man or a ruler. Whoever rides it will gain authority. Whoever is gored by it will be dismissed by the ruler. A fat ox indicates a fertile year.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The ox indicates a man of high ambition. Whoever sees an ox plowing the land will receive abundant goodness.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The ox is interpreted as a great man. Whoever sees himself fighting it is fighting a great man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The buffalo in a dream is a strong, patient, mighty man. Riding it indicates gaining authority.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The buffalo indicates a brave man who protects his family. Its milk is lawful money.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The buffalo is interpreted as a man of prestige. Whoever sees himself fighting it is disputing with a strong man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The rabbit in a dream is a woman, or it is said, a cowardly man. Whoever catches a rabbit will marry a woman. Eating its meat indicates gaining a small amount of wealth from a woman.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The rabbit indicates a woman of bad character. Whoever sees himself talking to a rabbit will fall into strife because of a woman.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The rabbit is interpreted as a woman. Whoever sees himself hunting one will get married.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The gazelle in a dream is a beautiful woman or a beautiful maidservant. Whoever hunts one will marry a free, beautiful woman. Its death indicates worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The gazelle indicates a beautiful child. Whoever sees himself slaughtering a gazelle is deflowering a virgin.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The gazelle is interpreted as a woman. Whoever sees himself eating its meat will gain wealth from a woman.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The sparrow is a man of amusement and falsehood, or a man of great stature and immense. Many sparrows indicate wealth and leadership. Plucking a sparrow's feathers indicates gaining wealth. Whoever sees himself eating sparrow meat will gain wealth from a great man.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The sparrow indicates a baby boy. Whoever catches a sparrow has gained control over a man of great stature. The sparrow's chirp indicates good speech or useful knowledge.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The sparrow is interpreted as a son or a servant. Whoever sees a sparrow fly from his hand, his son will die or his servant will leave. A slaughtered sparrow indicates achieving what one seeks from a great man after fatigue.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The falcon in a dream is a noble, brave ruler. Whoever owns an obedient falcon will gain authority and honor. The death of the falcon indicates the death of the king or the loss of his prestige.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The falcon indicates a knowledgeable, brave baby boy. Whoever sees himself hunting a falcon will be blessed with a blessed son.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The falcon is interpreted as the king or a noble man. Whoever sees himself carrying a falcon will serve a king and receive good from him.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The hawk in a dream is a ruler or a brave baby boy. Whoever sees himself carrying a hawk will gain authority and a son.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The hawk indicates an unjust, thieving man. Hunting it indicates victory over an enemy.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The hawk is interpreted as the king. Its death indicates the death of the king. Whoever sees himself eating its meat will gain wealth from a ruler.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The shaheen falcon in a dream is a ruler or a baby boy. It indicates a brave, formidable man.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The shaheen falcon indicates an unjust man. Hunting one indicates gaining authority from an unjust man.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The shaheen falcon is interpreted as the king or a noble man. Whoever sees that he owns one will gain authority and high status.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The owl in a dream is a tyrannical, fearsome king, or an arrogant thief of great might. It indicates unemployment and fear.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The owl indicates an envious man or a hateful woman. Its entry into the house indicates news of a death.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The owl is interpreted as a thief. Whoever sees himself fighting it is disputing with a thief.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The hoopoe in a dream is a knowledgeable writer, or a truthful messenger. Whoever owns one will gain a position or accompany a knowledgeable man.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The hoopoe indicates salvation from hardships. Seeing it indicates the arrival of an absent person or hearing good news.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The hoopoe is interpreted as a noble man. Whoever sees himself eating its meat will gain wealth from a noble man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The swallow in a dream is a faithful, ascetic man. Its entry into the house indicates blessing and goodness.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The swallow indicates a man who enjoins good and forbids evil. Whoever catches one will marry a righteous woman.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The swallow is interpreted as a righteous man. Seeing it indicates security and blessing.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The stork in a dream is a poor, needy man. It may also indicate the gathering of people for a matter of good or evil.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The stork indicates an ascetic man. Seeing it indicates travel and meeting loved ones.

interpretations.source: Al-Isharat fi Ilm al-Ibarat (Ibn Shahin)
interpretations.text: The stork is interpreted as a foreign man. Whoever sees that he owns one has befriended a foreign man.

interpretations.source: Tafsir al-Ahlam al-Kabir (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The ostrich in a dream is a Bedouin woman. Riding it indicates travel by land or committing an unlawful act. Its eggs indicate women.

interpretations.source: Ta'tir al-Anam fi Ta'bir al-Manam (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The ostrich indicates a blessing from God. Whoever owns one will gain authority over people from the desert.
