interpretations.text: A broken door is interpreted as a calamity concerning the head of the house.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with window and breaking) A broken window in a dream indicates scandal, exposure of a secret, or loss of status.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates worry and grief related to a woman or bad news.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and scandal.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A cracked wall in a dream indicates weakness in the man's condition, his illness, or the approach of his end.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A cracked wall indicates worries and problems in the family.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A cracked wall is interpreted as worry and illness.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: The collapse or falling of a ceiling in a dream indicates a great calamity from a great man or the death of the house's owner.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: The falling of a ceiling indicates the death of the father, husband, or master.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: The falling of a ceiling is interpreted as calamity and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Breaking a pillar in a dream indicates the death of the one it represents (like the leader, father, or religion).

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Breaking a pillar indicates the death of the ruler, father, or husband.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Breaking a pillar is interpreted as worry and calamity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Breaking a spear in a dream indicates the death of a child or brother, or weakness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Breaking a spear indicates removal from authority or failure.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Breaking a spear is interpreted as worry and calamity concerning a child.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with bow and cutting) A cut bowstring indicates difficulty in travel or the death of the one represented by the bow (like a child or wife).

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates inability and failure in a matter or separation.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and difficulty in affairs.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with arrow) A bent arrow indicates a false messenger, crooked speech, or failure to achieve a goal.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates a need not being met or difficulty in a matter.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and failure.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with shield) A pierced shield indicates weak protection or betrayal by a friend or brother.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates harm or damage occurring despite protection.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and fear.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with helmet and cracking) A cracked helmet indicates weakness in authority, loss of prestige, or danger threatening security.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates weakness in protecting family or husband.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and fear.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A torn banner in a dream indicates the dispersion of soldiers or the death of a scholar or leader.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A torn banner indicates loss of position or death of the husband.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A torn banner is interpreted as worry and calamity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Tearing the Quran in a dream indicates denying God's blessings and corruption in religion.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Tearing the Quran indicates committing a major sin or abandoning religion.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Tearing the Quran is interpreted as worry and misguidance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with pen and dryness) A dry pen in a dream indicates interruption of knowledge or authority, or difficulty in fulfilling needs.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates inability in management or inability to express oneself.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and disruption of affairs.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with inkwell and emptiness) An empty inkwell indicates poverty, infertility, or loss of knowledge.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates separation from a wife or servant, or not having a child.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as poverty and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with message and tearing) Tearing a message in a dream indicates severing a relationship, corruption of a matter, or news not arriving.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates worry and grief due to bad news or failure in a matter.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and severing relationships.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with seal and breaking) Breaking a seal in a dream indicates loss of authority or position, or exposure of a secret.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates failure in completing a matter or not achieving one's goal.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and loss of position.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Losing a key in a dream indicates difficulty in affairs and loss of help and sustenance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Losing a key indicates loss of knowledge, money, or a spy.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Losing a key is interpreted as worry and difficulty in affairs.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Opening a lock by force in a dream indicates overcoming difficulties and achieving one's goal after hardship.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Opening a lock by force may indicate taking someone's virginity or revealing a secret by force.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Opening a lock by force is interpreted as relief after hardship.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Breaking a chain in a dream indicates leaving religion, breaking a covenant, or separating from a wife or child.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Breaking a chain indicates relief from worry and salvation from hardship.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Breaking a chain is interpreted as the removal of sin or worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Breaking a fetter in a dream indicates leaving religion or relief from worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Breaking a fetter indicates salvation from prison, worry, or travel.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Breaking a fetter is interpreted as the removal of debt or worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Unlocking a yoke in a dream indicates repentance from disbelief or salvation from worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Unlocking a yoke indicates relief from hardship or separation from a bad wife.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Unlocking a yoke is interpreted as the end of worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Imbalance or tilting of a scale in a dream indicates tyranny, injustice, and corruption in religion.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Imbalance of a scale indicates misguidance or loss in trade.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Imbalance of a scale is interpreted as injustice and corruption of judgment.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An empty cup in a dream indicates a non-pregnant woman or unemployment and poverty.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An empty cup indicates disappointment or a need not being met.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An empty cup is interpreted as poverty and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An empty pitcher in a dream indicates a useless servant or a child with no good in him.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An empty pitcher indicates poverty or lack of knowledge.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An empty pitcher is interpreted as poverty and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An empty jar in a dream indicates poverty, death of a servant, or divorce of the wife.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An empty jar indicates a worthless secret or a matter that will not be completed.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An empty jar is interpreted as poverty and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An empty pot in a dream indicates the poverty or unemployment of the head of the household.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An empty pot indicates a ruler with no justice or a scholar with no knowledge.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An empty pot is interpreted as poverty and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A nephew (brother's son) in a dream indicates support and backing. Seeing him indicates strength or weakness depending on his state in the dream.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A nephew (brother's son) indicates a partner or a friend. Seeing him in a good state indicates goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A nephew (brother's son) is interpreted as goodness and benefit. Whoever sees him happy will attain joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A niece (brother's daughter) in a dream indicates relief, joy, and approaching goodness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A niece (brother's daughter) indicates a world approaching with goodness. Seeing her indicates the end of worry.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A niece (brother's daughter) is interpreted as goodness and joy. Whoever sees her will attain goodness.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A nephew (sister's son) in a dream is like a son, indicating support and help.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A nephew (sister's son) indicates joy and benefit coming from relatives.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A nephew (sister's son) is interpreted as goodness and benefit. Seeing him indicates strength for the dreamer.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A niece (sister's daughter) in a dream indicates relief and abundance in sustenance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A niece (sister's daughter) indicates a world approaching with goodness and blessing.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A niece (sister's daughter) is interpreted as goodness and joy. Whoever sees her will attain relief.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A grandson in a dream indicates extension of life, offspring, and approaching goodness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A grandson indicates joy and blessing in wealth and children.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A grandson is interpreted as goodness and benefit. Seeing him indicates an increase in sustenance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A granddaughter in a dream indicates a world approaching with goodness, blessing, and abundance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A granddaughter indicates relief, joy, and the end of worries.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A granddaughter is interpreted as goodness and joy. Whoever sees her will attain relief.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A paternal male cousin in a dream indicates kinship and support, and may indicate a partner or friend.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A paternal male cousin indicates a close man who benefits or harms depending on his state in the dream.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A paternal male cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit if he is in a good state.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A paternal female cousin in a dream indicates goodness coming from relatives or marriage within the family.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A paternal female cousin indicates joy and relief or partnership.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A paternal female cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A maternal male cousin in a dream indicates a friend or helper, and seeing him indicates comfort and reassurance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A maternal male cousin indicates a close man who offers help.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A maternal male cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A maternal female cousin in a dream indicates goodness and relief coming from relatives.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A maternal female cousin indicates joy and the end of worry.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A maternal female cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Marrying a second wife in a dream indicates abundance in sustenance or authority and position according to the woman's beauty.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Marrying a second wife may indicate worry and grief or a new partnership.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Marrying a second wife is interpreted as goodness, benefit, and abundance in the world.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased father in a dream may indicate weakness and feebleness for the dreamer, or indicate goodness coming from him if he is happy, or his need for prayers if he is sad. His words are true.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased father alive indicates relief, joy, and fulfillment of a need. If he gives something, it is good; if he takes something, it is a loss.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased father is interpreted according to his state. If laughing, he is in bliss; if crying, he needs prayers and charity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased mother in a dream indicates the arrival of mercy and relief. If she is sad, it indicates the dreamer's negligence towards her or in his religion. Her words are true.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased mother alive indicates relief from worry and grief and healing for the sick.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased mother is interpreted according to her state, and it indicates compassion and mercy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased brother in a dream indicates health and strength for the dreamer if the deceased is happy. If sad, it indicates weakness or worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased brother alive indicates the arrival of an absent person or gaining strength.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased brother is interpreted according to his state, and may indicate a partner or friend.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased sister in a dream indicates the arrival of an absent person or joy and relief.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased sister alive indicates the end of worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased sister is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased son in a dream indicates salvation from an enemy or the end of worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased son alive indicates the return of an old enemy.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased son is interpreted as the end of worry and salvation from an enemy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased daughter in a dream indicates despair of relief or severe worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased daughter alive indicates renewed hope and relief after despair.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased daughter is interpreted as worry and despair.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased husband in a dream indicates the woman's family scattering and her poverty if he is sad, or goodness reaching her if he is happy.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased husband alive indicates the righteousness of her condition or her marriage if she is eligible.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased husband is interpreted according to his state, and seeing him in a good state is good for the woman.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased wife in a dream indicates poverty, loss of position, or worry. Seeing her alive indicates the return of a despaired matter.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased wife alive indicates goodness and sustenance coming to the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased wife is interpreted as worry and poverty.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased friend in a dream indicates his need for prayers and charity. If he is happy, it indicates his good state and the dreamer's good state.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased friend alive indicates the arrival of good news or help.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased friend is interpreted as goodness and benefit if he is in a good state.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased neighbor in a dream indicates a change in the dreamer's fortune. If happy, his fortune improves; if sad, his fortune worsens.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased neighbor alive indicates goodness coming from the neighbors.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased neighbor is interpreted as goodness if he is in a good state.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased king in a dream indicates weakness of the state, ruin of the country, or injustice of the current ruler.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased king alive indicates the return of justice or the appearance of truth.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased king is interpreted as weakness and humiliation.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased scholar in a dream indicates the appearance of heresy or misguidance in that place.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased scholar alive indicates the spread of his knowledge and people being guided by it.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased scholar is interpreted as the spread of ignorance and misguidance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased rich person in a dream indicates the poverty of his family after him or his need for prayers.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased rich person alive indicates the return of wealth or sustenance.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased rich person is interpreted as his need for charity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased poor person in a dream indicates his comfort in the hereafter if he was righteous.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased poor person alive indicates relief and wealth for the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased poor person is interpreted as comfort and salvation.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased child in a dream indicates the end of worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased child alive indicates renewed worry or the return of a problem.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased child is interpreted as the end of worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry father in a dream indicates his dissatisfaction with the dreamer or the dreamer committing something that angers him.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry father indicates the child's disobedience or negligence towards him.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry father is interpreted as worry. Whoever sees his father angry will be afflicted with worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry mother in a dream indicates the dreamer committing a sin or negligence towards her.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry mother indicates God's displeasure or worry afflicting the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry mother is interpreted as worry. Whoever sees his mother angry will be afflicted with worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry husband in a dream indicates marital problems or negligence from the wife.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry husband indicates worry afflicting the woman from him.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry husband is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry wife in a dream indicates worries and problems in the house or negligence from the husband.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry wife indicates worry afflicting the man from her.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry wife is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry friend in a dream indicates a misunderstanding or disagreement between them.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry friend indicates worry afflicting the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry friend is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing enemy in a dream indicates his gloating and the dreamer falling into calamity or worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing enemy indicates worry and grief afflicting the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing enemy is interpreted as worry and calamity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A friend crying in a dream (without screaming) indicates joy and happiness for him or the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A friend crying indicates his need for help or that he is going through hardship.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A friend crying is interpreted as relief and joy for him.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) father in a dream indicates his satisfaction, happiness, and the fulfillment of the dreamer's wishes.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing father indicates goodness and benefit attained by the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing father is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) mother in a dream indicates relief, mercy, and approaching goodness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing mother indicates the end of worries and good tidings.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing mother is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) brother in a dream indicates strength, support, and goodness coming from him.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing brother indicates joy and benefit.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing brother is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) sister in a dream indicates the arrival of an absent person or joy and relief.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing sister indicates goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing sister is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing child in a dream indicates good news and imminent relief.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing child indicates the end of worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing child is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A crying child in a dream indicates worry, grief, and fatigue.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A crying child indicates hard-heartedness or the occurrence of injustice.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A crying child is interpreted as worry and strife.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's father in a dream indicates disobedience or opposing his command.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's father indicates worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's father is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's mother in a dream indicates committing a sin or negligence towards her.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's mother indicates severe worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's mother is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's brother in a dream indicates cutting family ties or disagreement in partnership.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's brother indicates worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's brother is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's husband in a dream indicates marital disagreements or instability.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's husband indicates worry and grief for the woman.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's husband is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's wife in a dream indicates worries and problems in the house or loss.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's wife indicates worry and grief for the man.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Arguing with one's wife is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Arguing with a friend in a dream indicates separation or a misunderstanding that could lead to enmity.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Arguing with a friend indicates worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Arguing with a friend is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Arguing with a stranger in a dream indicates falling into dispute or strife.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Arguing with a stranger indicates worry and grief coming from an unexpected source.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Arguing with a stranger is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Eating dirt in a dream indicates extreme poverty and need, or death.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Eating dirt indicates gaining wealth proportionate to the amount eaten.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Eating dirt is interpreted as wealth. Whoever sees himself eating it will gain wealth.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Eating stone in a dream indicates striving for a very difficult matter or disputing with a hard-hearted man.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Eating stone indicates gaining wealth with extreme difficulty.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Eating stone is interpreted as worry and fatigue.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Eating glass in a dream indicates bearing worries and troubles related to women or exposing secrets.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Eating glass indicates hurtful speech or strife.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Eating glass is interpreted as worry. Whoever sees himself eating it will be afflicted with worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Eating paper in a dream indicates seeking and memorizing knowledge, or gaining wealth proportionate to what is written on it, if written.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Eating paper indicates memorizing knowledge or concealing testimony.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Eating paper is interpreted as wealth or knowledge. Whoever sees himself eating it will gain wealth or knowledge.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Eating coal in a dream indicates consuming unlawful money from a ruler or a dangerous man.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Eating coal indicates falling into worry or giving false testimony.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Eating coal is interpreted as unlawful money or worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Eating ashes in a dream indicates false speech, unlawful money, or striving for a useless matter.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Eating ashes indicates knowledge not acted upon, or worry and regret.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Eating ashes is interpreted as worry and grief.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Eating clay in a dream indicates backbiting, slander, consuming the deceased's money, or unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Eating clay indicates illness or worry.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Eating clay is interpreted as worry and illness.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Drinking human blood in a dream indicates gaining wealth and benefit from that person, or salvation from their evil if they are an enemy.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Drinking blood indicates unlawful money or sin.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Drinking blood is interpreted as unlawful money or committing a sin.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Drinking urine in a dream indicates unlawful money or falling into doubt.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Drinking human urine indicates gaining suspicious money. Drinking animal urine indicates benefit.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Drinking urine is interpreted as unlawful money or worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Being drunk from wine in a dream indicates fear, ignorance, loss of blessings, and gaining unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Drunkenness indicates unemployment and heedlessness. It may indicate security from fear.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Drunkenness is interpreted as worry and committing a sin.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Drinking poison in a dream, if it does not harm the dreamer, indicates gaining wealth or long life.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Drinking poison and not dying from it indicates piety and devotion, or salvation from worry.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Drinking poison and not dying is interpreted as salvation from worry or wealth.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Drinking bitter medicine in a dream indicates recovery from illness if sick, or indicates poverty and need if healthy.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Drinking bitter medicine indicates repentance or advice that one dislikes.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Drinking bitter medicine is interpreted as healing or worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Drinking salty seawater in a dream indicates gaining wealth from a ruler with worry and fatigue.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Drinking seawater indicates vast knowledge or abundant wealth.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Drinking seawater is interpreted as gaining wealth from the king.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Walking on air in a dream indicates arrogance and falsehood if the dreamer is not righteous. If righteous, it indicates exaltation and a blessed journey.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Walking in the air indicates travel, fame, or righteousness in religion.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Walking in the air is interpreted as travel or exaltation.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Walking on fire in a dream indicates committing sins and major offenses or wading into great strife.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Walking on fire indicates victory over enemies or striving for a dangerous matter.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Walking on fire is interpreted as worry and strife.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Walking on thorns in a dream indicates falling into hardship, debt, or mixing with evil people.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Walking on thorns indicates worry, grief, and fatigue in seeking livelihood.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Walking on thorns is interpreted as worry and fatigue.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Walking backwards in a dream indicates retreating from a matter, corruption in religion, and change of condition for the worse.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Walking backwards indicates regret over a past matter or abandoning work.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Walking backwards is interpreted as worry and change of condition for the worse.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with running) Walking quickly in a dream indicates quick fulfillment of needs and salvation from a fearful matter.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates serious striving in an important matter.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as quick fulfillment of needs.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Walking slowly in a dream indicates weakness, cowardice, or illness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Walking slowly indicates hesitation in a matter or fear of it.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Walking slowly is interpreted as worry and weakness.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Dancing in the mosque indicates mocking religion and falling into heresy.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Dancing in the mosque indicates calamity and worry.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Dancing in the mosque is interpreted as worry and misguidance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Dancing in the market indicates scandal and loss of modesty.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Dancing in the market indicates worry, grief, and loss.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Dancing in the market is interpreted as worry and scandal.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Dancing alone in a closed place is less worrying than dancing in front of people.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Dancing alone indicates minor worry or short-lived joy.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Dancing alone is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Screaming in the market indicates strife or loss in trade.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Screaming in the market indicates worry, grief, and scandal.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Screaming in the market is interpreted as worry and loss.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Screaming in the mosque indicates heresy or a calamity afflicting religious people.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Screaming in the mosque indicates worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Screaming in the mosque is interpreted as worry and heresy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Screaming over the dead indicates following their way if they were righteous, or indicates calamity and worry if accompanied by wailing and slapping.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Screaming over the dead indicates worry and sadness.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Screaming over the dead is interpreted as worry and calamity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Singing in the bathroom indicates ugly speech and immorality.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Singing in the bathroom indicates worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Singing in the bathroom is interpreted as worry and committing a sin.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Singing in the mosque indicates mocking religion and misguidance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Singing in the mosque indicates strife and heresy.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Singing in the mosque is interpreted as worry and misguidance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Reciting the Quran backwards indicates abandoning religion, following desires, and misguidance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Reciting the Quran backwards indicates committing heresy or speaking falsehood.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Reciting the Quran backwards is interpreted as misguidance and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Reciting the Quran without purity indicates disrespecting religion or non-acceptance of deeds.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: It may indicate memorizing the Quran by heart or knowing it.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: It is interpreted as disrespecting religion.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Praying without ablution indicates non-acceptance of deeds or striving for a false matter that will not be completed.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Praying without ablution indicates illness or loss in trade.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Praying without ablution is interpreted as worry and loss.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Praying facing away from the Qibla indicates committing a great sin, misguidance in religion, or abandoning the Sunnah.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Praying facing away from the Qibla indicates Hajj if it is during the Hajj months, or indicates confusion in religion.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Praying facing away from the Qibla is interpreted as committing a major mistake or misguidance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Praying in an impure place indicates corruption in religion and committing abominations.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Praying in an impure place indicates worry and grief or unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Praying in an impure place is interpreted as worry and corruption.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Giving the Adhan at the wrong time indicates strife, the appearance of a strange matter, or heresy.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Giving the Adhan at the wrong time indicates slander or spying.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Giving the Adhan at the wrong time is interpreted as worry and strife.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Giving the Adhan in the bathroom indicates disrespecting religion or severe illness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Giving the Adhan in the bathroom indicates fever or ugly speech.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Giving the Adhan in the bathroom is interpreted as worry and illness.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Performing Hajj outside its months indicates loss in trade or corruption in religion.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Performing Hajj at the wrong time indicates striving for a false matter that will not be completed.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Performing Hajj at the wrong time is interpreted as worry and loss.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Performing Tawaf in the reverse direction indicates committing heresy or opposing the Sunnah.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Performing Tawaf in the reverse direction indicates misguidance in religion.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Performing Tawaf in the reverse direction is interpreted as misguidance and worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with standing and solitude) Standing at Arafat alone may indicate an answered prayer in seclusion or sincere repentance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It may indicate withdrawing from people for worship or worry and loneliness.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as good if for worship, and as worry if for loneliness.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Stoning the Jamarat with large pebbles may indicate paying off a large debt or overcoming a strong enemy.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It may indicate exaggeration in a matter or exceeding the limit.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as paying off debt or victory.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Sacrificing a defective animal indicates non-acceptance of deeds, deficiency in religion, or unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Sacrificing a defective animal indicates worry and grief or not fulfilling a vow.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Sacrificing a defective animal is interpreted as worry and non-acceptance of deeds.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: (By analogy with eating raw meat) Eating raw sacrificial meat indicates backbiting family and relatives or unlawful money.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It indicates worry, grief, and illness.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: (By analogy) It is interpreted as worry and backbiting.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Wearing dirty Ihram indicates committing a sin, corruption in intention, or non-acceptance of Hajj or Umrah.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Wearing dirty Ihram indicates worry, grief, and illness.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Wearing dirty Ihram is interpreted as worry and sin.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Cutting or shaving hair before exiting Ihram indicates not completing the rituals or committing a prohibition.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: It indicates opposing the Sunnah or non-acceptance of deeds.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: It is interpreted as worry and negligence in worship.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A grandson in a dream indicates extension of life, offspring, and approaching goodness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A grandson indicates joy and blessing in wealth and children.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A grandson is interpreted as goodness and benefit. Seeing him indicates an increase in sustenance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A granddaughter in a dream indicates a world approaching with goodness, blessing, and abundance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A granddaughter indicates relief, joy, and the end of worries.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A granddaughter is interpreted as goodness and joy. Whoever sees her will attain relief.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A paternal male cousin in a dream indicates kinship and support, and may indicate a partner or friend.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A paternal male cousin indicates a close man who benefits or harms depending on his state in the dream.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A paternal male cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit if he is in a good state.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A paternal female cousin in a dream indicates goodness coming from relatives or marriage within the family.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A paternal female cousin indicates joy and relief or partnership.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A paternal female cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A maternal male cousin in a dream indicates a friend or helper, and seeing him indicates comfort and reassurance.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A maternal male cousin indicates a close man who offers help.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A maternal male cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A maternal female cousin in a dream indicates goodness and relief coming from relatives.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A maternal female cousin indicates joy and the end of worry.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A maternal female cousin is interpreted as goodness and benefit.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Marrying a second wife in a dream indicates abundance in sustenance or authority and position according to the woman's beauty.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Marrying a second wife may indicate worry and grief or a new partnership.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Marrying a second wife is interpreted as goodness, benefit, and abundance in the world.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased father in a dream may indicate weakness and feebleness for the dreamer, or indicate goodness coming from him if he is happy, or his need for prayers if he is sad. His words are true.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased father alive indicates relief, joy, and fulfillment of a need. If he gives something, it is good; if he takes something, it is a loss.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased father is interpreted according to his state. If laughing, he is in bliss; if crying, he needs prayers and charity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased mother in a dream indicates the arrival of mercy and relief. If she is sad, it indicates the dreamer's negligence towards her or in his religion. Her words are true.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased mother alive indicates relief from worry and grief and healing for the sick.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased mother is interpreted according to her state, and it indicates compassion and mercy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased brother in a dream indicates health and strength for the dreamer if the deceased is happy. If sad, it indicates weakness or worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased brother alive indicates the arrival of an absent person or gaining strength.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased brother is interpreted according to his state, and may indicate a partner or friend.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased sister in a dream indicates the arrival of an absent person or joy and relief.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased sister alive indicates the end of worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased sister is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased son in a dream indicates salvation from an enemy or the end of worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased son alive indicates the return of an old enemy.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased son is interpreted as the end of worry and salvation from an enemy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased daughter in a dream indicates despair of relief or severe worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased daughter alive indicates renewed hope and relief after despair.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased daughter is interpreted as worry and despair.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased husband in a dream indicates the woman's family scattering and her poverty if he is sad, or goodness reaching her if he is happy.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased husband alive indicates the righteousness of her condition or her marriage if she is eligible.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased husband is interpreted according to his state, and seeing him in a good state is good for the woman.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased wife in a dream indicates poverty, loss of position, or worry. Seeing her alive indicates the return of a despaired matter.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased wife alive indicates goodness and sustenance coming to the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased wife is interpreted as worry and poverty.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased friend in a dream indicates his need for prayers and charity. If he is happy, it indicates his good state and the dreamer's good state.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased friend alive indicates the arrival of good news or help.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased friend is interpreted as goodness and benefit if he is in a good state.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased neighbor in a dream indicates a change in the dreamer's fortune. If happy, his fortune improves; if sad, his fortune worsens.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased neighbor alive indicates goodness coming from the neighbors.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing one's deceased neighbor is interpreted as goodness if he is in a good state.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased king in a dream indicates weakness of the state, ruin of the country, or injustice of the current ruler.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased king alive indicates the return of justice or the appearance of truth.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased king is interpreted as weakness and humiliation.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased scholar in a dream indicates the appearance of heresy or misguidance in that place.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased scholar alive indicates the spread of his knowledge and people being guided by it.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased scholar is interpreted as the spread of ignorance and misguidance.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased rich person in a dream indicates the poverty of his family after him or his need for prayers.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased rich person alive indicates the return of wealth or sustenance.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased rich person is interpreted as his need for charity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased poor person in a dream indicates his comfort in the hereafter if he was righteous.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased poor person alive indicates relief and wealth for the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased poor person is interpreted as comfort and salvation.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased child in a dream indicates the end of worry and grief.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased child alive indicates renewed worry or the return of a problem.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: Seeing a deceased child is interpreted as the end of worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry father in a dream indicates his dissatisfaction with the dreamer or the dreamer committing something that angers him.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry father indicates the child's disobedience or negligence towards him.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry father is interpreted as worry. Whoever sees his father angry will be afflicted with worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry mother in a dream indicates the dreamer committing a sin or negligence towards her.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry mother indicates God's displeasure or worry afflicting the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry mother is interpreted as worry. Whoever sees his mother angry will be afflicted with worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry husband in a dream indicates marital problems or negligence from the wife.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry husband indicates worry afflicting the woman from him.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry husband is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry wife in a dream indicates worries and problems in the house or negligence from the husband.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry wife indicates worry afflicting the man from her.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry wife is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: An angry friend in a dream indicates a misunderstanding or disagreement between them.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: An angry friend indicates worry afflicting the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: An angry friend is interpreted as worry.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing enemy in a dream indicates his gloating and the dreamer falling into calamity or worry.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing enemy indicates worry and grief afflicting the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing enemy is interpreted as worry and calamity.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A friend crying in a dream (without screaming) indicates joy and happiness for him or the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A friend crying indicates his need for help or that he is going through hardship.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A friend crying is interpreted as relief and joy for him.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) father in a dream indicates his satisfaction, happiness, and the fulfillment of the dreamer's wishes.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing father indicates goodness and benefit attained by the dreamer.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing father is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) mother in a dream indicates relief, mercy, and approaching goodness.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing mother indicates the end of worries and good tidings.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing mother is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) brother in a dream indicates strength, support, and goodness coming from him.

interpretations.source: Perfuming Humanity in the Expression of Dreams (Al-Nabulsi)
interpretations.text: A laughing brother indicates joy and benefit.

interpretations.source: Signs in the Science of Expressions (Ibn Shaheen)
interpretations.text: A laughing brother is interpreted as goodness and joy.

interpretations.source: The Great Interpretation of Dreams (Ibn Sirin)
interpretations.text: A laughing (smiling) sister in a dream indicates the arrival of an absent person or joy and relief.
